text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Residents of cholera-infested Lochnivar area have resisted government moves to evacuate the flooded Kafue plains to safer areas posing a possible rise in the death toll from the disease.
_ The Zambian Airforce has appealed to government to improve conditions of service to gain more loyalty from personnel.

- Deputy finance minister Reverend Dan Pule has said that Zambia's programme with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank was still on course and the contribution of the two multi-lateral institutions would be part of this year's budget.

- The Zambia Congress Of Trade Unuions predicted that the new year will be tougher for workers than 1996 and called on employees to be united and speak with one voice to overcome numerous hurdles ahead.
- Defence minister Ben Mwila has called on Zambian soldiers to be more alert in guarding the country in the wake of military upheavals in neighbouring states.
- UNIP president Kenneth Kaunda has vowed that his party will ensure the current government is removed and fresh elections held before the end of the year.

- Government will redefine its policies on agricultural credit arrangements and the marketing system so peasent farmers are not continually impoverished, agriculture, food and fisheries minister Edith Nawakwi said.
